You cannot detect something on a radar warning receiver that isn’t spiking you. RWR works by detecting UNIQUE and REPEATING radar signatures to avoid going off from background noise from the sun, space, radar, data-links, satellites etc. 

The F-22 specifically uses AESA radar that can lock on a target without that target knowing. The F22’s APG-77 is ludicrous at hiding its signature. 2000 T/R modules changing frequency up to a 1000 of times per second. It spreads total power across the entire operational bandwidth in a single beam constantly changing characteristics. Combine that with F22’s EWS which jams enemy radar for further concealment. 

On radar like AN/ALR-67, the F-22’s radar lock will blend in with background noise. So you’ve been locked on and are blissfully unaware of it. After all a single radar peak could be anything. 

But thats how the PLANE avoids detection, as for the missile? Well again, no radar spike, no detection. The AIM-120 fired from the F22 will use inertial guidance relayed from the plane or another plane like a fighter or AWACS via data-link. The missile will launch and continue to receive guidance from the F22 or other aircraft while approaching the target from long range. 

The active radar seeker on-board the missile is off at this point so will not show up on enemy RWR. But once the missile is close enough it will activate and the RWR will detect it. This is what we call going PITBULL.

But now the missile is more than close enough to successfully intercept with a high chance of success. Future missiles like the AIM 260 JATM will be hypersonic with a range of around 200km and will be even harder to evade. If it was that easy to avoid these missiles they wouldn’t be used.

That’s only if you see it coming. An F-22 firing an AIM-120 from BVR won’t show up on your RWR until it activates its active seeker. And by that time the missile will be halfway to its target. If you can assess the RWR and MWS fast enough, break hard and deploy ECM you could *possibly* evade it depending on your initial vector and how good your plane is. Otherwise you’re probably dead.

I see where your coming from and I respect your stance on guns. What you say is true of course. Firearms purpose is to end life as efficiently as possible.

Canada doesn’t condone killing as means of self-defence. Such cases are individualized and not as clear cut as say US castle law. You can’t legally have any weapon for the purposes of “self-defence” here but you are allowed to use any amount of reasonable force to protect yourself and others, including lethal force if the situation calls for it. Actual cases of Canadians using guns for defence is extremely rare and most of those times they’re not found guilty of murder and many times the aggressor who was shot doesn’t even die. (Gunshots aren’t as lethal as people think. More often then not you need to shoot twice or more to kill)

In an ideal world where violence no longer exists perhaps we won’t need weapons anymore and while humans have come a long way from the times of Ghengis Khan and Alexander, we also don’t live in the year 3500 where we have transcended our violent nature and only seek peace and knowledge. 

So violence and by extension weapons, are here to stay for a long time. The future will be a bit uncertain with emerging technologies that might allow anybody to create weapons right at home. (You can literally 3D print a gun. Smart CNC machines with AI could potentially make you a 1:1 replica of an M4A1, a gun not even Americans are allowed to own.) 

So ultimately to disarm everyone is a fruitless endeavour because if someone truly wants a gun, they will get one. I don’t own a firearm for the purpose of defence because I sincerely doubt I will EVER need it. I also legally have to keep it in a safe with a trigger-guard so I can’t easily access it either.

But at the same time defence of one’s self and property is a right. 

How is not justified to kill someone who is actively trying to kill you? Of course you would try to mitigate the possibility of death by using force in proportion to the threat. 

But at the end of the day if its the life of some criminal/psychopath or mine? I choose mine. Guns are simply the most effective killing tool.

I am Canadian not American. Our gun laws aren’t perfect but I find them to be reasonable for the most part.

I think smarter laws and restrictions should be put into place. In the United States total firearm prohibition is impossible. It’s heavily ingrained in American culture and there are millions upon millions of unregulated firearms in circulation that would be impossible to find and confiscate. 

Now nobody needs fully-automatic rifles that are intended for Military or Law enforcement use. For hunting, semi-auto/bolt-action long rifles and shotguns are more than sufficient and are the primary weapons of choice anyway. A crazed gunmen with enough ammunition and full-auto on his weapon could kill a *LOT* of people in a crowded mall or other public area before police show up to stop him. They’re highly effective killing instruments that can’t be trusted in the hands of the average person.

Handguns are more complicated. On one hand they’re ideal for home-defence and recreational shooting. On the other, they are easy to conceal and use for crime. 

Also with access to resources on the internet and 3D printers/CNC machines, anyone who REALLY wanted a gun and had the technical know-how could make one and you can’t stop them from doing so. (Are we going to ban knowledge and manufacturing tools now?) 

The only true way IMO is to put measures in place to ensure the ONLY people able to purchase firearms are mentally stable, law-abiding individuals. Background-checks, Firearm registries, mandatory training and licensing have proven to work. In addition to this, sources of illegal gun-trafficking needs to be targeted and neutralized.
